newsitem.title: USA: Texaco forms independent equality task force.
newsitem.headline: Texaco forms independent equality task force.

text.p: Texaco Inc said Monday it has formed an independent equality and fairness task force to monitor improvements in the giant oil company's human resources programs.
The task force is headed by Deval Patrick, a former U.S. assistant attorney general who headed the Justice Department's civil rights division between 1994 and 1996.
Patrick is curently a partner at the Boston, Mass., law firm of Day, Berry & Howard.
The task force was formed as part of a $176-million settlement Texaco reached in November 1996 of a racial discrimination lawsuit filed against it by six black employees in 1994, the company said.
The seven members of the panel were selected by Texaco and plaintiffs' counsel, it said.
- John Gibbons, a retired chief judge of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit and currently professor at Seton Hall University Law School, Newark, N.J.;
- Jeffalyn Johnson, president and chief executive officer, Integrated Quality Solutions Inc, Alexandria, Va.;
- Allen Krowe, Texaco vice chairman, who is retiring from the company on June 30;
- Mari Matsuda, professor, Georgetown University Law Center, Washington, D.C.;
- Luis G. Nogales, president, Nogales Partners, Los Angeles; and
- Thomas Williamson, partner at the Covington & Burling law firm, Washington, D.C.
